notes.note: Uses mtc.killed inside a PTC; 'mtc' is not an ObjectReference in the BNF, so rejection may come from syntax rather than a dedicated semantic check. Applying killed to a component variable that holds the MTC reference can only be detected at runtime and is not covered.
Reject test as in ETSI NegSem_210308_killed_operation_010 (array with an uninitialized element in straight-line code). Titan accepts it because it does not track element initialization statically.
Ambiguous 'dimension': a 3x3 array with an index array of size 1 is used, which violates both readings (number of dimensions = 2, size of a dimension = 3).
Repeated invocation is made observable by killing a lower-index component after the any from killed operation; a re-evaluation would yield index 0 instead of 2.
Titan does not implement the call operation on test components (V4.17.1 feature); its syntax errors are expected. Applies to all accept tests of 21.3.10 that use call (tests 001-010, 038-042).
An infinite timeout cannot be proven; the test only shows that a call without a timeout waits for a 2 s behaviour to complete instead of timing out.
Reading 1 chosen; only functions are tested (an early return statement and reaching the end of the body). Complete execution of called altsteps is not covered.

'From MTC only' is tested as a reject test with the operation inside a function started on a PTC, following ETSI NegSem_210303_Stop_test_component_002. Titan does not check this statically. Same for tests 018, 022, 026, 030 and 034.

Reading 1 chosen; the violation is treated as a test case error (runtime), as in the example of the standard. Only the 'non-alive component called twice' case is tested, not a call on a killed component.
